SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 5-day history of dry cough (≈ every 20–30 min) and constant streaming nose with green discharge. Associated intermittent feeling of being “very hot” with chills, myalgia. Brief episode of diarrhoea at onset, now resolved.
- Review of symptoms: Denies sputum production, chest pain, shortness of breath, pleuritic pain, haemoptysis, sore throat, otalgia, headache, visual changes, rash, current vomiting or diarrhoea.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications:
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Lisinopril – dose unclear (“200” stated)  
  • Lemsip (paracetamol-containing cold remedy) 2–3 sachets/day  
  • Occasional cough syrup at night (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies: No known drug allergies; reports mild seasonal hay fever.
- Social history: Lives with partner and dog; employed as office manager. Occasional alcohol (“odd sherry”). Smoking status not stated.

Objective:
- No face-to-face examination performed (teleconsultation).
- Vitals: Not measured; patient subjectively feels febrile.
- No additional physical findings or investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute cough / upper respiratory tract infection
   - Assessment: Likely viral upper respiratory infection/bronchitis.
   - Differential: Early bacterial chest infection, COVID-19, influenza.
   - Investigations planned: Purchase thermometer, monitor and record temperature.
   - Treatment planned: Continue Lemsip (contains paracetamol); avoid other paracetamol-containing products. Maintain hydration. Use small amount of cough syrup only at night if sleep-disturbing.
   - Safety-net advice: Re-consult urgently if temperature ≥ 37.5–38 °C persists or spikes, cough worsens or becomes productive/purulent/bloody, haemoptysis, nasal bleeding, chest pain, or shortness of breath. Possible need for antibiotics if bacterial infection suspected.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
   - Assessment: Established T2DM; recent blood test (≈ 3 weeks ago) reportedly normal.
   - Investigations planned: Continue routine diabetes monitoring with GP; consider home glucose monitoring if equipment obtained.
   - Treatment planned: Continue metformin.

3. Hypertension
   - Assessment: Established hypertension; current BP control uncertain.
   - Investigations planned: Arrange routine blood pressure check with GP.
   - Treatment planned: Continue lisinopril; confirm correct dose with prescribing team.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Confirm smoking status; verify exact doses/frequencies of metformin and lisinopril; objective vitals (BP, HR, temp, SpO₂); documented allergy list beyond patient recall; recent BP and HbA1c results.  
• Internal conflicts: None significant—green nasal discharge suggests bacterial element whereas clinician impression viral (noted).  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional incomplete responses; medication dose for lisinopril uncertain (“200” stated).
